draft.title: Flexibility training
card: Flexibility is the range of movement at a joint. Stretching trains it, and the type of stretch should suit the time and the sport.
Static
a stretch held still at the end of the range, often for 15 to 30 seconds. It is used after training or in a session aimed at gaining range.
Dynamic
controlled movements that take a joint through its full range, such as leg swings. They are often used in a warm-up, before sports that need movement.
Ballistic
fast, bouncing movements that push past the normal range. They carry a higher risk of injury, so they suit trained athletes in sports such as gymnastics or martial arts.
PNF
a partner helps stretch a muscle, the person contracts it against resistance, then relaxes and stretches further. It can give large gains in range but needs a partner or trained person.
draft.remember: Flexibility is trained by stretching, and each type suits a different time, sport or level of skill.

a.q: Which stretch takes a joint through its full range using controlled movement, such as leg swings?
opts: Dynamic stretching
Static stretching
Ballistic stretching
PNF stretching
a.why: Dynamic stretching uses controlled movement through the full range. Ballistic stretching is the tempting wrong answer because it also moves, but it uses fast bouncing movements that push past the normal range.
a.clue: Think of controlled movement, not bouncing or holding still.

b.q: Priya plays netball and wants to loosen her hips before a match. Which stretch best suits this, and why?
opts: Dynamic, because it moves joints through range before play
Static, because holding a stretch is the best way to prepare
Ballistic, because bouncing gives the largest gain in range
PNF, because a partner can stretch her during the match
b.why: Dynamic stretching suits a warm-up because it moves the joints through their range in a controlled way. Static stretching is the tempting wrong answer, but it is held still and suits after training or a session aimed at gaining range.
b.clue: Which type uses controlled movement and suits a warm-up?

b.best: Dynamic, because it moves joints through range before play

Dynamic
controlled movements that take a joint through its full range, such as leg swings. They are often used in a warm-up, before sports that need movement.
Ballistic

proposal.remember: Flexibility is range of movement at a joint. Pick the stretch that suits the time, the sport and the athlete.

a.q: Why is ballistic stretching usually kept for trained athletes?
opts: It pushes past the normal range, so injury risk is higher
It is held still for a long time, so beginners tire
It needs a partner, so beginners cannot do it alone
It uses slow movement, so it only suits a cool-down
a.why: Ballistic stretching bounces past the normal range of movement, which raises the risk of injury. Needing a partner is tempting, but that describes PNF, not ballistic stretching.
a.clue: Think about what each type risks, not how it is set up.

b.q: Priya's netball team has ten minutes on court before the first centre pass. She wants her hips ready for quick lunges and changes of direction. Which stretch suits this time best?
opts: Dynamic, as it moves joints through range with control
Static, as long holds give the biggest gain in range
PNF, as contracting then relaxing gives large gains
Ballistic, as bouncing movements copy the speed of netball
b.why: Priya is warming up, and dynamic stretching is the type used in a warm-up for sports that need movement. PNF is tempting because it gives large gains, but it suits a session aimed at gaining range, not the minutes before a game. Ballistic carries a higher injury risk and suits trained athletes in sports like gymnastics.
b.clue: Gaining the most range is not her goal in the next ten minutes.
